batch_strategy: Measure controlled ratio and loading comparisons where completion remains unresolved, test remaining strong-eluent endpoint dips, and check reproducibility in the inconsistent cinnamate region. Extend these questions to related carbonyl and amino-ester families so the labels teach transferable structure-condition responses.

choices.reason: m81 under pure EA at 111 mg forms a controlled loading comparison with the selected 166.5 mg row. Measured 5/1 completions differ substantially between fefecd79dc057980f62c at 111 mg and a9500e468002e41eceeb at 166.5 mg, whereas current pure-EA predictions are nearly loading-invariant. This tests whether the loading association extends to the strong-eluent baseline.

m81 under pure EA at 166.5 mg anchors the high-loading curve before measured 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1 records 06c0c99f1cfb752ed34b, bee82d193ec1ce4fde27 and a9500e468002e41eceeb. Paired with the selected 111 mg baseline, it tests whether short high-loading completion is condition-specific.

m81 at 5/1 and 55.5 mg connects recent low-loading 1/1 measurement fa5d86f56c1c38fa9416 to the 5/1 completion difference between fefecd79dc057980f62c at 111 mg and a9500e468002e41eceeb at 166.5 mg. A third loading level tests the relationship without assuming that loading always broadens elution.

m81 at 10/1 and 166.5 mg is predicted to finish near 16.86 mL, compared with measured 9.23 mL at 5/1 in a9500e468002e41eceeb. It tests whether the high-loading curve develops substantial completion growth after 5/1 while onset remains early, using identical loading conditions.

m33 under pure EA at 99.7 mg supplies an intermediate loading level between 17fd49e7bf1b8c8b08f7 at 49.85 mg and 003ad1a9637ac1b7c0fd at 149.55 mg. Their completions differ despite early onsets. This also supplies a matched-loading baseline for recent 1/1 and 10/1 measurements.

m33 at 5/1 and 99.7 mg is predicted to finish near 12.63 mL, below measured 15.02 mL at 1/1 in 7a9775ac62acbc27a73d and 19.32 mL at 10/1 in b08821181fbd4d81b247. This controlled intermediate point distinguishes a genuine completion dip from an incorrectly compressed response curve.

m115 at 1/1 and 162 mg anchors the early curve before recent 2/1 measurement d1ea63515e645b84e0cd, whose completion was underpredicted by 8.07 mL at acquisition. Matching loading and DCM volume helps determine whether the correction belongs to the baseline or subsequent ratio response.

m115 at 2/1 and 108 mg tests loading transfer from d1ea63515e645b84e0cd at 162 mg and connects to same-loading 10/1 observation 68f56b81e86e40c37d6b. Its current completion prediction near 20.42 mL tests an early plateau rather than assuming continued growth of both endpoints.

m128 under pure EA at 150 mg establishes the missing strong-eluent baseline for recent 2/1 observation 34aaca6f7a0768d743fe and measured 5/1 and 10/1 rows 91cd087e44e7a3364533 and 596bd04bfe916866f908. It locates the beginning of the sulfur-containing ketone response and separates baseline from slope learning.

m128 at 2/1 and 50 mg tests whether the approximately 21 mL completion measured at 150 mg in 34aaca6f7a0768d743fe transfers across loading. Same-loading 1/1 observation b655d7de0986cbd0d622 and 5/1 observation cdcabd704ebeeeca9183 constrain the local curve; current predictions are almost loading-insensitive here.

m183 at 5/1 and 152.85 mg bridges same-loading 2/1 observation 7296174cea3ffd8ac464 and the selected 20/1 row. Recent cdd3b7758b3405a7b53f and cf5c7a2e1940e3c09dd5 showed a much larger weak-eluent response than the acquisition model predicted. This tests where that response develops at another load.

m183 at 20/1 matches the selected 5/1 loading and PE/300 uL conditions. Its current prediction is approximately 19.68/31.03 mL. Together with 7296174cea3ffd8ac464 and recent 101.9 mg measurements, it tests the corrected response shape and its transfer across loading.

m134 at 2/1 and 96.2 mg is predicted to finish near 10.52 mL, below measured 12.51 mL at 1/1 in 6fe77425f0d00758ebb8 and 14.57 mL at 5/1 in 5fe9702f3a3a783b4c94. The previous weak-eluent onset collapse was disproved; this matched-loading point tests the remaining early completion dip.

m185 at 2/1 and 131.7 mg tests the predicted rapid completion increase from measured pure-EA 8.26 mL in 90986ae76102a348680d to approximately 17.87 mL. Same-loading 10/1 measurement f3ee8cbdb15889a1a50d finished at 18.65 mL. This locates an otherwise unmeasured early transition.

m185 at 5/1 matches the selected 2/1 and 20/1 rows. Predicted completion near 18.95 mL is almost equal to the measured 10/1 endpoint in f3ee8cbdb15889a1a50d. Measuring this point tests the proposed intermediate plateau and whether the recent completion correction transfers between ratios.

m185 at 20/1 and 131.7 mg extends measured 10/1 record f3ee8cbdb15889a1a50d at fixed loading and DCM volume. The current 13.09/23.72 mL prediction tests renewed growth after the proposed plateau; lower-loading 50/1 observation 6c28e50241ca84637c9f provides context without establishing loading invariance.

Ortho-amino ester m89 at 1/1 and 111.7 mg forms a fixed-loading pair with the selected 2/1 row. Predicted completion is about 15.02 mL. Recent 2/1 observation 0141de34d99a6428ddd7 finished at 10.83 mL at 167.55 mg, motivating a controlled test of the early dip and its loading dependence.

m89 at 2/1 and 111.7 mg matches the selected 1/1 conditions and adds a second loading level to recent 0141de34d99a6428ddd7. Its predicted completion near 11.89 mL tests whether short 2/1 completion transfers across loading, while same-loading 10/1 record c6a55a8d89f33c69899b anchors later growth.

Methyl ortho-amino ester m104 at 1/1 and 58.4 mg supplies an uncovered early anchor matched to measured 2/1 record a2b3a77e1b5200f7c164 and 5/1 record 9333d130f52d80332cf0. Its predicted completion near 13.85 mL tests an early minimum and positional/ester transfer without introducing a loading confound.

m72 at 5/1 and 102.2 mg completes a controlled early curve with recent pure-EA and 1/1 records 71f5df8c7d7e88d1afce and d90d024730eb01bff3c7, plus initial 2/1 record 2466da143763ef5563ef. It measures the transition toward broader completion at fixed DCM/200 uL conditions.

Sterically substituted ketone m29 under pure EA at 97.5 mg is predicted at approximately 6.36/19.92 mL, later than its selected 2/1 prediction. Same-loading 5/1 record 60880ddea87941f6e9ca and 50/1 record f73fd2f4c55177304721 constrain the weaker-eluent curve. This tests an uncovered baseline with substantial quantile spread.

m29 at 2/1 matches the selected pure-EA conditions but is predicted to finish near 8.02 mL rather than 19.92 mL. The pair directly tests this large predicted completion decline. Comparison with m33 can teach substituent-environment effects, with their different loading solvents retained explicitly.

Fluorene-containing ketone m38 under pure EA at 150 mg supplies a missing baseline, predicted near 7.27/19.53 mL with high CW distance. It forms a controlled comparison with the selected 2/1 row. Measured lower-loading 5/1 and 10/1 records bfcb567664468f0d6902 and 86fb9a8fd6633397d670 provide response references.

m38 at 2/1 matches the selected pure-EA conditions and is predicted near 5.53/14.64 mL, earlier for both endpoints. The pair discriminates a real strong-eluent response from an unanchored baseline artifact and extends learning beyond the simpler aromatic ketones in recent feedback.

Salicylaldehyde m197 at 2/1 and 114.6 mg is predicted to finish near 17.29 mL, compared with measured 25.53 mL at 1/1 in 69be7348f9ab10739164. This tests an unmeasured completion dip in an ortho phenol-aldehyde environment; possible intramolecular interactions are a chemical prior, not an established mechanism.

m197 at 5/1 matches the selected 2/1 conditions and links them to same-loading 10/1 observation 04e162e0c1261108b4a0. Lower-loading 5/1 observation a91850e587e062097c02 finished near 24.51 mL. The new point tests recovery after the predicted dip and distinguishes ratio response from loading transfer.

m73 under pure EA at 100 uL checks the inconsistent cinnamate baseline: current prediction is approximately 10.10/13.64 mL, while near-identical b187c8a6f7beb2c7f61f measured 4.39/9.42 mL. This is a near repeat: density 1.0491 versus 1.049 changes derived loading by 0.01 mg. Pairing with 1/1 tests response reproducibility.

m73 at 1/1 matches the selected pure-EA conditions and nearly repeats initial 2cf789c87f7c6325c020, which measured a narrow 18.60/18.96 mL interval. Lower-loading 1/1 records 7bd4e959319ef8b7b0fe and a387411cbcb6be48bde4 also disagree. The pair tests reproducibility before extending this behavior to related esters.

Phenylmalonate m75 at 1/1 and 54.75 mg anchors an uncovered early response before the selected 2/1 point. Same-loading 10/1 and 20/1 observations ce3b9d9cbe1699c7eef9 and 3726956d81fe3954e5b7 provide later anchors. It tests aromatic malonate completion relative to the narrow strong-eluent intervals measured for m80.

m75 at 2/1 matches the selected 1/1 conditions. Predicted completion changes little, from approximately 11.16 to 11.38 mL, despite substantial later growth in ce3b9d9cbe1699c7eef9 and 3726956d81fe3954e5b7. This pair locates the early response and provides a neutral multi-ester comparison for m81.

Dioxole-containing ketone m39 at 1/1 and 100 mg fills a strong-eluent gap before same-loading 5/1 observation 8aa79ce56a84843f3849. Its approximately 15.02 mL completion prediction has a broad quantile span and high CW distance. The selected 2/1 point makes this a local response experiment.

m39 at 2/1 matches the selected 1/1 conditions, with predicted completion near 18.48 mL. Together with measured 5/1 record 8aa79ce56a84843f3849 and pure-EA reference 89fc4c70c5a2e9ea04d3 at higher loading, it locates early growth for an oxygen-rich aromatic ketone and tests transfer from methoxy and thioether families.

hypotheses.content: Neutral carbonyl completion needs structure-, ratio- and loading-specific responses separate from onset. m33 retains early onset with changing completion, while m81 shows short completion at 166.5 mg across 1/1–5/1 and longer completion in some lower-loading records. The reproducibility and extent of the m81 association remain unresolved; it does not establish a universal loading mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Opposing historical completion errors and nearly loading-invariant current predictions suggest that a shared shift of V1 and V2 misses useful relationships. Controlled labels can identify endpoint-specific interactions that transfer across carbonyl rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m81 loading contrast persist under pure EA, and where does its high-loading completion begin to grow? Does m33 show the predicted 5/1 completion dip at fixed loading?

hypotheses.content: The large m80 completion increase from 52.75 to 105.5 mg at 1/1 is a reproducible loading response. This interpretation of the original gap is rejected by the repeat and additional loading level; modest loading dependence remains possible.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The exact 105.5 mg repeat finished at 7.03 mL instead of 15.66 mL, and the 158.25 mg row finished at 8.03 mL. The original broad record should not motivate a deterministic large loading slope across malonates.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: If this region is revisited later, what is the within-tuple completion dispersion? The present batch instead examines the m81 association, which has several consistent high-loading observations.

hypotheses.content: Aldehyde ratio response is structure-specific. Recent m183 and m134 labels establish substantial weak-eluent growth and disprove the predicted m134 early-onset collapse. They do not resolve m134's predicted 2/1 completion dip or the predicted early-rise, intermediate-plateau pattern for m185.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The recent failures distinguish incorrect slopes from baseline errors. Intermediate and matched-loading extensions can teach where retention growth develops without transferring one aldehyde curve indiscriminately to another.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m183's corrected curve transfer to 152.85 mg, does m134 finish earlier at 2/1 than at 1/1, and how much of m185's completion increase occurs before 5/1?

hypotheses.content: The m128/m115 comparison requires endpoint-specific substituent-by-ratio responses. At the measured 2/1 settings, m128 starts later but both compounds finish near 21.5 mL, weakening the previous predicted completion contrast. Their different density-derived loads prevent attribution to sulfur substitution alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A substituent correction that moves both endpoints together would miss the newly measured contrast. Early anchors and additional 2/1 loading levels test whether onset and completion relationships generalize across oxygen- and sulfur-containing ketones.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does the early response begin for each ketone, and does the near-equal 2/1 completion persist across additional loading levels?

hypotheses.content: Ortho-amino ester and amino/enamino ester rows need distinct early completion responses. The short m89 2/1 interval differs from para and meta references under their recorded conditions, while matched m72 measurements show later completion at 1/1 than under pure EA. Predicted early dips in m89 and m104 remain untested; intramolecular hydrogen bonding is only a chemical prior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These compounds share several coarse polarity descriptors but differ in nitrogen environment and measured response. Local early curves can improve positional and functional-group transfer while retaining loading-solvent differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the fixed-111.7 mg m89 1/1-to-2/1 pair confirm a completion decline, and does short 2/1 completion transfer across loading? Does m104 show an early minimum, and does m72 continue its measured growth at 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Strong-eluent completion need not follow a universal monotonic rule: measured m164 finishes earlier at 1/1 than under pure EA. The analogous predicted declines for m29, m38 and m197 may be real endpoint responses or unanchored model compression and require controlled measurements.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Several large predicted declines occur in uncovered early curves. Resolving them teaches when onset and completion respond differently and avoids imposing a chemical prior as an absolute constraint.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the matched m29 and m38 pure-EA/2/1 pairs reproduce their predicted declines, and does m197 show a 2/1 minimum between measured 1/1 and newly measured 5/1?

hypotheses.content: The m73 strong-eluent region contains inconsistent labels, including reversed endpoints and substantially different outcomes at repeated tuples. Its apparent exceptional condition response may combine reproducible behavior with label variability; the available evidence does not identify the cause.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An inconsistent region can distort the learned ester baseline and ratio response. Paired near repeats provide information about reproducibility instead of interpreting every anomalous endpoint as a deterministic structural effect.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At approximately 104.91 mg and DCM/300 uL, do pure-EA and 1/1 measurements reproduce the ordinary pure-EA interval and unusually narrow later 1/1 interval?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes reject several predicted reversals while strengthening endpoint-specific planning. m134 measured 7.09/19.67 mL at 20/1 and 9.95/27.78 mL at 50/1, disproving its predicted onset collapse. m183 showed much stronger weak-eluent growth than predicted; current predictions have adapted, so the next labels target intermediate response and loading transfer. m185 completion was overpredicted by 6.64 and 7.45 mL at acquisition under pure EA and 10/1, motivating its uncovered early curve. The m128/m115 2/1 comparison yielded nearly equal completion, 21.33 versus 21.62 mL, despite different onsets, weakening the prior completion contrast. m33 completion was underpredicted at both selected ratios, while m81 low-loading 1/1 completion was underpredicted and high-loading 5/1 completion overpredicted; a generic correction or loading-broadening rule would be inappropriate. The m80 exact repeat finished at 7.03 mL versus the original 15.66 mL, and the higher-load row finished at 8.03 mL, rejecting the large reproducible loading-slope interpretation. Matched m72 and m213 labels did not confirm their predicted pure-EA-to-1/1 completion dips. m71's measured interval was about 6.06 mL rather than the predicted 0.36 mL. The m45 pure-EA completion was 8.56 mL, and its negative-V2 weak-eluent record remains an unexplained anomaly. Historical acquisition errors are not current-model residuals. No new labels were revealed during this catalog correction.
batch_rationale: The 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs cover 16 already observed molecules through compact experiments with specific learning questions. m81 and m33 address persistent completion failures and loading interactions. The sulfur/methoxy ketones test the revised endpoint-specific interpretation of the recent substituent comparison. Aldehyde and amino-ester rows locate early transitions, plateaus and possible minima using measured anchors. m29, m38 and m197 test conspicuous strong-eluent predictions in distinct structural environments, while the m73 pair checks reproducibility in an inconsistent region. m75 and m39 extend early-response coverage to related neutral multiacceptor families with useful later anchors. Multiple rows per molecule are justified by controlled comparisons; duplicate candidate tuples are otherwise avoided. Quantile spans and CW distance are secondary diagnostics from the single predictor, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and elution interval width is treated as a target relationship rather than uncertainty. The batch may improve generalization across the Row-distribution by supplying transferable structure-ratio-loading relationships and clarifying misleading local patterns, without selecting for maximal retention or chromatographic performance.
